The rest of the Watch section renders only when `watchConnected || watchDeviceName != null`; otherwise it shows one of two hint cards ("Watch app installed but not nearby..." or "Install the GlycemicGPT Wear app on your watch via sideloading..."). `WatchFaceGalleryCard`: a horizontally scrolling row of `WatchFaceVariant` entries — DIGITAL_FULL ("Digital", "BG, IoB, graph, and time with all overlays", all four overlays default true) and ANALOG_MECHANICAL ("Analog", "Classic analog with deep navy dial and silver hands", all four overlay defaults FALSE) — each 100dp wide with a 2dp primary border when selected; selecting a variant ALSO resets the four overlay toggles to that variant's defaults. A "Push <name> Face" Button disabled while pushing. `pushWatchFace()` guards with an `AtomicBoolean` compareAndSet, cancels any auto-dismiss job, and runs `withTimeout(PUSH_TIMEOUT_MS = 150_000L)`; a timeout becomes `Result.Error("Push timed out")`, a CancellationException returns state to Idle and rethrows, other exceptions become `Error(message)`. Success/Error render an inline row with a Dismiss button and auto-dismiss after `AUTO_DISMISS_MS = 5_000L`. `WatchFaceConfigCard`: toggles "Show IoB", "Show Glucose Graph", "Alert Vibration", "Show Seconds"; a Graph Range FilterChip row of 1H/3H/6H; a Theme radio group (Dark→`THEME_DARK`, Clinical Blue→`THEME_CLINICAL_BLUE`, High Contrast→`THEME_HIGH_CONTRAST`); and — only when `showGraph && selectedVariant.hasGraph` — four Graph Overlay toggles ("Basal Rate Area", "Bolus Markers", "IoB Overlay", "Activity Mode Bands"). `updateWatchFaceConfig` coerces `graphRangeHours` to one of `VALID_GRAPH_RANGES = [1, 3, 6]` (falling back to 3), persists every field to `AppSettingsStore` (theme persisted by LABEL, variant by enum NAME), and syncs to the watch. The sync sends the theme's `contractKey` (not the label) and pulls `aiTtsEnabled`/`aiTtsVoice` from the canonical store rather than the config copy, to avoid overwriting a value set from the chat screen; it then also syncs bolus category labels. `WatchAppUpdateCard` state machine: `Idle → Checking → (Available | UpToDate | Error)`; `Available → Downloading → Pushing → Installing → Success | Error`. `checkForWatchUpdate()` no-ops while Checking or within `WATCH_UPDATE_CHECK_COOLDOWN_MS = 10_000L` of the last check, errors with "Watch version not available" when `watchVersionCode == null`, and reads channel/dev-build/version from the DataLayer in one pass before calling `WearAppUpdateChecker`. After a successful APK push it enters `Installing` and starts a 15_000ms timer that flips to `Success` if still Installing. The downloaded wear APK file is deleted in a `finally`. `WatchDataTelemetryCard` shows "Last BG sent (wire, mg/dL)" and "Last IoB sent" (`%.2fU`) with a relative age; the BG value is VALIDATED to `20..500` and shown as null otherwise; telemetry reads are wrapped in `withTimeout(TELEMETRY_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000L)` and any failure shows "Could not read watch data". `formatTimeAgo`: negative → "just now"; <60_000 → "just now"; <3_600_000 → "<m>m ago"; <86_400_000 → "<h>h ago"; else "<d>d ago".
edge_cases: The telemetry BG label explicitly says "(wire, mg/dL)" because the watch always receives canonical mg/dL regardless of the user's display unit — labeling it prevents it being read as a UI value.
A persisted watch-face variant name that no longer exists falls back to DIGITAL_FULL with a warning log.
`persistWatchFaceConfig` deliberately does NOT write `aiTtsEnabled` from the config copy.

capabilities.name: Settings — Appearance: theme mode and glucose units
capabilities.behavior: Theme card: title "Theme" / "Choose your preferred color scheme" and three equal-weight OutlinedButtons (System / Dark / Light, tags `theme_system`, `theme_dark`, `theme_light`) where the selected one is filled with `primary`/`onPrimary`. `ThemeMode` is PER-DEVICE, persisted as the enum name in `theme_mode` (default System, corrupt values fall back to System). The color schemes are fixed (no Material You): dark = Slate950 bg / Slate900 surface / Slate800 surfaceVariant / Blue600 primary / Red500 error; light = Slate50 bg / White surface / Slate100 surfaceVariant / same primary and error. Glucose Units card: title "Glucose Units" / "Choose how glucose values are displayed across the app"; two buttons "mg/dL" and "mmol/L" (tags `glucose_unit_mgdl`, `glucose_unit_mmol`), selected one filled. A one-time smart-default notice appears above them when `seedNeedsConfirm` (tag `glucose_unit_seed_notice`): Info icon + "We set this to <unit> based on your region or your Nightscout. Change it anytime below." + a "Got it" TextButton (tag `glucose_unit_seed_dismiss`) — it never blocks the UI. `setGlucoseUnit(unit)` writes the local cache optimistically, clears the sync error AND the seed notice, and — only when a backend is configured — PATCHes `/api/settings/glucose-unit`, folding a differing server-resolved unit back into the selector; a PATCH failure keeps the optimistic value and shows "Saved on this device. Couldn't sync to your account." In BLE-only mode the local write is the whole save (no PATCH, no error). `dismissGlucoseUnitSeedNotice()` clears the local flag immediately then best-effort `POST /api/settings/glucose-unit/acknowledge` (which stamps provenance "user" server-side so the notice never recurs); a failed ack leaves it hidden for the session. `seedNeedsConfirm` is reconciled from `GET /api/settings/glucose-unit` as `glucose_unit_source == "seed" && unit != MGDL`. Unit conversion is centralized in `GlucoseFormat` with `MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156` ("the exact glucose mass-to-molarity factor and the single canonical constant ... Never introduce a second value (18.02 / 18.0182); a drift here desyncs the client from the server"); mg/dL renders as an integer, mmol/L as `%.1f` in Locale.US, converting ONCE from the most precise mg/dL source and rounding LAST so 70→3.9, 180→10.0, 120→6.7, 100→5.6. A glucose SPREAD (standard deviation / difference) uses `convertSpread` (offset-free) — reusing the value converter for a spread is documented as a bug.
edge_cases: Storage, transport, every threshold comparison, alert detection, and the platform-wide 20-500 safety invariant all stay canonical mg/dL — the unit only selects display and speech.
`glucoseUnitFlow()` and `mealIntelligenceEnabledFlow()` are SharedPreferences-listener callbackFlows so display surfaces update live.
Wire values are "mgdl"/"mmol"; unknown/null falls back to MGDL.

capabilities.name: Settings — About section (version info, licenses entry, in-app self-update)
capabilities.behavior: Card with an Info icon + "App Info" and three `InfoRow`s: "Version" = `BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME`, "Build" = `BuildConfig.BUILD_TYPE`, "BLE Protocol" = `"<protocolName> v<version>"` from the active pump plugin or "None". Then a full-width "Open Source Licenses" TextButton with a trailing KeyboardArrowRight icon (tag `open_source_licenses_button`) navigating to the licenses route. Then a divider and the update state machine: `Idle` → "Check for Updates" button; `Checking` → spinner + "Checking for updates..."; `UpToDate` → CheckCircle + "You are on the latest version" + "Check Again"; `Available` → "Update available: v<version>", "Size: <X.X> MB" (bytes / 1024 / 1024, one decimal), up to 3 lines of release notes, and a "Download & Install" + "Later" row; `Downloading` → spinner + "Downloading update..."; `ReadyToInstall` → "Install Update" button that starts the FileProvider install intent; `Error` → the message in error color + a "Retry" button. `checkForUpdate()` no-ops while already Checking. `AppUpdateChecker` uses a STANDALONE OkHttp client (no auth/baseUrl interceptors) with connect 15s / read 60s and polls GitHub: stable = `https://api.github.com/repos/lumose-health/android-unofficial/releases/latest`, dev = `.../releases/tags/dev-latest`, chosen by `BuildConfig.UPDATE_CHANNEL`. HTTP 403 → "Rate limit exceeded. Try again later."; 404 on dev → "No dev release available yet."; other → "GitHub API returned <code>". Stable compares a parsed version code against `BuildConfig.VERSION_CODE`; dev compares a run number parsed from the asset name via `Regex("-dev\\.(\\d+)-")` against `BuildConfig.DEV_BUILD_NUMBER`. `downloadApk` enforces `https://` in CODE (not just network_security_config, since cleartext is now globally permitted for the LAN opt-in) → "Download blocked: insecure URL", and restricts the host to `{github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com}` → "Download blocked: untrusted host"; it sanitizes the filename, deletes all previously downloaded APKs, and verifies `apkFile.length() == expectedSize` (deleting the file and erroring on mismatch). The install intent is `ACTION_VIEW` on a FileProvider URI with mime `application/vnd.android.package-archive` and GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION | NEW_TASK. The wear checker mirrors this with a 100 MB (`100L * 1024 * 1024`) download cap and asset prefix `GlycemicGPT-Wear-`.
edge_cases: Distribution is GitHub Releases (sideload), not the Play Store — "open source diabetes software, not FDA approved".
The APK download is treated as a code-execution path and therefore gets https + host allowlist + exact-size verification.

capabilities.name: Settings — Battery Optimization card

capabilities.behavior: Registered as `Screen.BleDebug("ble_debug")` only inside `if (BuildConfig.DEBUG)`; it is a spoke route (no bottom nav). Each entry card shows TX (primary) / RX (tertiary), the opcode name, the opcode as `(0x<hex padded to 2>)` in 11sp monospace, an `HH:mm:ss.SSS` timestamp in the system zone, a `txId=<n>  cargo=<n>B` line, horizontally scrollable monospace cargo hex, and any parsed value (primary) or error (error color). Injection constants: `TEST_CGM_MG_DL = 120`, `TEST_LOW_CGM_MG_DL = 54`, `TEST_STALE_AGE_SECONDS = 60L` (past the compressed debug policy's 45s TOO_STALE bound), `SEED_SYNC_EVENT_COUNT = 20`. `injectCgm(mgDl, ageSeconds)` is hard-gated with `if (!BuildConfig.DEBUG) return` as defense-in-depth ("this writes to the same Room cache that drives the real glucose hero and can fire a real OS alarm"), builds a `CgmReading(glucoseMgDl, CgmTrend.FLAT, Instant.now().minusSeconds(age))`, saves it via `PumpDataRepository.saveCgm`, and then drives `PumpPollingOrchestrator.processCgmReading` — the exact production seam `pollCgm` uses — so the watch relay and alert floor see it identically to a polled reading. `seedSyncQueue()` starts `PumpConnectionService` (so the drain loop exists on an emulator), then enqueues 20 `BasalReading(rate = 0.5f, isAutomated = true, activityMode = NONE)` with distinct per-second timestamps through `SyncQueueEnqueuer.enqueueBasalBatch` (whose backend-configured gate still applies); failures are logged, never crash. `BleDebugStore` is an in-memory circular buffer of `CAPACITY = 100` entries whose mutating operations are no-ops in release (R8 eliminates them).
edge_cases: The stale-LOW injection is the SAFETY test: with the compressed policy the alert floor must SUPPRESS and the surface must say "NOT watching" (GLY-115 AC2).
The fresh-LOW injection must FIRE the floor (GLY-115 AC1/AC10) — a real OS alarm on a real device.

capabilities.name: In-app Open Source Licenses viewer
capabilities.behavior: `LicensesScreen(onBack)` inside `DetailScaffold(title = "Open Source Licenses")`. State machine: `Loading` (centered spinner) → `Loaded` | `Unavailable`. Assets are read on `Dispatchers.IO` in a `LaunchedEffect(assets)`; an `IOException` logs "License assets are missing from this build" and yields `Unavailable`, rendering "License text could not be read from this build." in error color (this is a packaging failure, not a user state). The `rememberLazyListState` is HOISTED ABOVE the loading branch so a rotation returns the reader to their position instead of the top of a 35 KB document. Loaded content is wrapped in ONE `SelectionContainer` around the whole list (not per item) "because selection has to be able to cross paragraph boundaries for copying a clause to be of any use", inside a `LazyColumn` with 16dp content padding and 12dp spacing, in this order: the project notice (markdown), divider, the third-party attributions (markdown), divider, one item PER LICENSE FAMILY of the generated runtime-dependency document, divider, one item per paragraph of the runtime dependency license texts (PLAIN text), divider, one item per paragraph of the full GPL-3.0 (PLAIN text). Markdown items pass `linkifyMask = 0` (these documents name files, not sites) and `isTextSelectable = true` (they render into a view SelectionContainer cannot reach). Paragraph splitting uses `Regex("\\n\\s*\\n")`; section splitting keeps each `## ` heading with the section it introduces. `stripUnresolvableLinks` reduces repository-relative markdown links to their label text via `Regex("(?<!!)\\[([^\\]]+)]\\((?![a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.\\-]*:)[^)]*\\)")` — targets carrying a URI scheme (e.g. `mailto:`) are left alone because "a mailto: address is information a reader may need out of a licensing document". The five bundled assets are `licenses/project_license_notice.md`, `licenses/third_party_licenses.md`, `licenses/runtime_dependencies.md`, `licenses/runtime_dependency_licenses.txt`, `licenses/gpl-3.0.txt`. They are regenerated into the APK on EVERY build by the `generateLicenseAssets` Gradle task from `README.md`'s `## License` section (excerpted verbatim up to the next `## `; a missing heading FAILS the build), the root `LICENSE`, `docs/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md`, and two documents produced by `generateDependencyAttribution` from the resolved RELEASE runtime graph of every APK-shipping module. An empty source document fails the build rather than shipping a blank licence section. Entry point is the "Open Source Licenses" row in Settings > About; the whole screen works with NO connectivity.
edge_cases: License texts are rendered as PLAIN text, never markdown, because "their numbered clauses parse as list markers and their indented lines as code blocks".
The GPL is split per paragraph so the list measures only what is on screen instead of all ~670 lines.
The screen states NOTHING of its own about how the project is licensed — every word comes from a bundled document.

safety_critical: MEAL CARB ESTIMATES ARE NEVER A DOSE. `VERIFY_BEFORE_DOSING_TEXT` = "Rough estimate — an AI guess that's often wrong. Never use it to calculate an insulin dose or bolus." must accompany EVERY carb estimate surface: the Log-a-Meal result (pinned above the scroll region so it can never scroll away), the meal history list header, the common-foods list header, the Re-log dialog, the Edit-common-food dialog (embedded inside the modal because the AlertDialog scrim dims the screen-level one), and the Home Recent-meal card. Domain KDoc calls the posture NON-NEGOTIABLE. Test tag `meal_safety_qualifier`; UI-tested by VerifyBeforeDosingQualifierUiTest.

Carbs are ALWAYS rendered as a low/high range plus a confidence signal, never a lone integer. A single-point estimate still renders as "≈ N g carbs". Nothing in the meal contract carries insulin, units, or a bolus by design.

Accessibility merge: `CarbEstimateContent` merges the carb value + confidence + safety qualifier + dispersion note into ONE content description so a screen reader can never announce the number without the never-dose qualifier.

Carb input bounds (client-side, mirroring the backend's reject-not-clamp): 0.0–1000.0 g, low <= high, NaN rejected. Invalid input NEVER reaches the API and is NEVER silently clamped. Shared by the food-record correction and common-food edit paths so the rules cannot drift.

Alert threshold validation (SETTINGS, BLE-only editor): all four values must be within 20–500 mg/dL and satisfy urgentLow <= low < high <= urgentHigh. Inputs are parsed in the user's display unit and stored canonically in mg/dL via `value * 18.0156` rounded. `AlertThresholdStore.updateLocal/updateAll` re-validate with `require()` as defense-in-depth and use `commit()` (synchronous). A backend threshold response that fails validation is DROPPED, never clamped, leaving last-known-good values.

Alert threshold arming: the on-device alert floor NEVER fires off the hardcoded defaults (55/70/180/250) — `isConfigured()` requires a real source (BACKEND sync or LOCAL editor save). Until then the Settings copy says, in ERROR color, "On-device alarms are OFF until you set all four thresholds."

Backend is master for alert thresholds: with a server configured the Settings editor is READ-ONLY, and `saveLocalAlertThresholds` re-checks `authRepository.isBackendConfigured()` LIVE (not the cached UI flag) and returns without writing. Saving a server URL flips the editor read-only in the same state update.

Logout clears BACKEND alert thresholds (disarming the floor so it can never fire off another account's values) but PRESERVES LOCAL ones. `clearBaseUrl()` on the BLE-only onboarding path does the same, so a now-server-less user is not left with a departed server's thresholds armed.

POST_NOTIFICATIONS is requested on BOTH onboarding completion paths — after login AND after "Use without a server (BLE-only)". Code comment: "Requesting POST_NOTIFICATIONS here is safety-critical: the on-device alert floor is silently suppressed without the permission, so a tier-1 user could later believe they are monitored when they are not."
Settings Notifications card states, in ERROR color when the permission is missing: "Disabled -- alerts will not appear on your phone".

Low and High glucose alert channels are created with `setBypassDnd(true)` unconditionally, independent of the "Boost Volume for Lows" toggle; the toggle only raises alarm-stream volume for lows. Low alerts use `setOnlyAlertOnce(false)` so the sound re-fires on every update ("Lows are life-threatening").

Changing an alert sound DELETES and recreates the notification channel with an incremented version (Android channel sounds are immutable). This happens under `channelLock`, and `incrementChannelVersion` is a non-atomic read-modify-write that REQUIRES that lock — a race would produce duplicate channel versions and could leave alerts posting to a deleted channel.

Glucose unit conversion uses the single canonical constant `MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156` with a written prohibition on introducing a second value (18.02 / 18.0182). Conversion happens ONCE from the most precise mg/dL source and rounds LAST. A glucose SPREAD must use `convertSpread` (offset-free), never `convertValue` — reusing the value converter for a spread is documented as a bug.

Watch telemetry BG is validated to 20..500 mg/dL and shown as null outside that range, and its label explicitly reads "Last BG sent (wire, mg/dL)" so a canonical wire value is never misread as a display-unit value.

Debug fault injection (`simulateBackendUnreachable`, `debugFastStaleness`) and the BLE-debug CGM injectors are HARD-GATED to debug builds at the store getter/setter AND again inside the ViewModel (`if (!BuildConfig.DEBUG) return`) because injections write to the same Room cache that drives the real glucose hero and can fire a real OS alarm.

Debug LOW injections are the alert-floor safety harness: a FRESH 54 mg/dL must FIRE the floor; a 54 mg/dL aged 60s (past the compressed policy's 45s TOO_STALE bound) must be SUPPRESSED with the surface reading "NOT watching".

`UrlSecurityPolicy` is the SOLE guard preventing a public host from being reached over plaintext http:// (network_security_config permits cleartext globally for the LAN opt-in and cannot express CIDR ranges). It never performs DNS (DNS-rebinding defense), parses only strict canonical IP literals, and requires an explicit acknowledged opt-in plus a private/LAN host. Enabling insecure LAN HTTP is gated behind an acknowledgement dialog and surfaces a persistent app-wide banner.
AI chat and meal-photo estimates never surface raw exception messages; every failure path maps to curated copy (unit-tested: "never surfaces a raw exception message on unexpected failures").

The onboarding disclaimer page cannot be swiped past — only the explicit "I Understand" button advances it — and it includes a dedicated card naming the prohibited action for photo carb estimates: "Never use a photo carb estimate to calculate an insulin dose or bolus."

Meal photo uploads strip ALL EXIF/GPS metadata by re-encoding the bitmap (defense-in-depth on top of server-side stripping), and the transient full-resolution capture file is deleted after upload or on cancellation.
Every upload/compression failure path — including `OutOfMemoryError` — clears `isUploading`, so the "Estimating carbs…" spinner can never get permanently stuck on a medical surface.
Meal history / common foods show a terminal error state with Retry when the backend is unreachable, explicitly NOT a misleading "No meals logged yet." empty state.

AI chat TTS always appends ". This is not medical advice." to the spoken response, and the chat screen carries a permanent footer "AI responses are informational only. Always consult your healthcare provider."
`AppMarkdownText` strips all image markdown and `` tags from AI-generated content to prevent outbound image fetches, and only opens http/https links.

map.notes:
DELIBERATE DECISIONS AND GAPS THAT ARE LOAD-BEARING FOR THE PORT:

1. THERE IS NO AI DAILY BRIEF SCREEN. The backend has `/api/ai/briefs` in `contract/openapi.json`, but it is NOT declared in `GlycemicGptApi` and no client code fetches or renders briefs. The only in-app manifestation is the "AI Notifications" notification channel (description literally "AI analysis insights and daily briefs"), which receives any server-pushed alert whose type is neither a LOW nor a HIGH type. The onboarding Features page promises daily briefs; the Settings AI-sound row is the only control. If the iOS PRD wants a brief surface, it is NEW work, not a port.

2. AI chat has NO transcript persistence. Messages live only in the ViewModel (capped at the last 100), so process death or leaving the tab loses history. There is also no streaming — a single request/response with a 90s read timeout.

3. AI chat is backend-only by design. The tab is absent in BLE-only mode and the route redirects to Home. The watch relay refuses with terminal copy that deliberately never says "try again": "AI chat needs a GlycemicGPT server — none is set up on your phone."

4. Phone chat has NO speech-to-text; only the watch has voice input. Both have TTS, configured from ONE shared pair of settings (`aiTtsEnabled`, `aiTtsVoice`) that the phone pushes to the watch inside the watch-face config payload.

5. Meal "Re-log a common food" is READ-ONLY by documented API limitation: "The API has no create-record-from-common-food path (a record needs a photo upload), so this read-only sheet surfaces the saved carb range to verify, without persisting a new record. Lays the seam for record creation when the backend supports it."

6. Meal data has NO local cache and NO offline mode — history, common foods, and estimates are backend-only, which is why every meal screen has an explicit terminal offline state with Retry rather than a misleading empty state. Pagination is not implemented (fixed limit 50, offset 0).

7. The meal result screen shows the LOCAL photo thumbnail only; the backend returns no image, which is why the Home Recent-meal card uses a neutral Restaurant-icon placeholder.

8. Meal deletes (records and common foods) have NO confirmation dialog; plugin deactivate/remove and pump unpair DO.

9. `MealDispersion` and `suggestedIdentity` exist ONLY on the create response and are absent on history reads — history rows can never show the uncertainty treatment.

10. Two-layer gating is used throughout for meal intelligence: a local per-account cache for instant UI response (no round-trip) plus a server probe as the authoritative guard. The local cache defaults ON (mirroring the server), and both the PATCH and the GET FAIL CLOSED on 401/403 so meal surfaces cannot stay visible for an account the backend rejects.

11. Stale-response guards are used in three places and should be ported: meal identity/audit responses are discarded when `state.record?.id != requestRecordId`; the meal-intelligence PATCH uses a monotonically increasing request version plus job cancellation; meal-history and common-foods loads re-check `isActive` after the call because "a repository that wraps errors in Result can swallow the CancellationException".

12. Settings honest-failure copy is a deliberate pattern: `SETTING_SYNC_FAILED_MESSAGE` = "Saved on this device. Couldn't sync to your account." — chosen because the local save persists, the sync did not, and NOTHING re-PATCHes it later, so the copy promises neither.

13. Settings uses row-level and card-level BLE-only gates (GLY-146) rather than hiding whole sections: Backend Sync card hidden but Data Retention kept; the AI Notification sound row hidden but Low/High kept; the Meal Intelligence section hidden entirely; the Nightscout plugin's activation control withheld unless already active; the alert-threshold editor switched from read-only to editable.

14. The license viewer states nothing of its own — every word is a bundled asset regenerated from the repository's documents on every build, and the redistributed-component list is derived from the resolved RELEASE dependency graph so "a dependency cannot enter the build without entering the attribution". License texts render as plain text, never markdown. Works fully offline.

15. Onboarding's connection test PERSISTS the typed URL before it resolves (so BaseUrlInterceptor routes to it) and restores the previous URL on failure. `continueWithoutServer()` must therefore CANCEL the in-flight test BEFORE clearing the base URL — that ordering is explicitly load-bearing.

16. Onboarding start-destination policy is keyed on `onboardingComplete` ALONE, deliberately independent of session validity, so an expired refresh token during a long offline stretch cannot re-onboard a user and lock local Room-served pump data behind an impossible login.

17. The Home meal FAB is draggable with per-device persistence; bounds are enforced at PLACEMENT time (not on write) so a stale offset self-corrects against the live container, and there is a TalkBack custom action ("Reset position to default") because drag is pointer-only.

18. The confidence bar distinguishes Medium from Low by LENGTH, not color (they share the same amber) — an accessibility decision that must survive the port.

19. The safety qualifier and net-carb/sugar caveats deliberately use a soft-amber "calm caution" palette, NEVER error red, so a standing note is not mistaken for an alarm. `safetyPalette()` reads darkness off the active color scheme luminance so it tracks a FORCED theme mode.

20. Numbers a Swift engineer will need verbatim: chat max message 2000 chars / max transcript 100; chat read timeout 90s vs default 15s; watch chat max query 500 chars, watch timeout 30s, wearable await timeout 10s, phone relay API timeout 90s; image max dimension 1280 px, max bytes 5 MiB, JPEG quality 90→40 in steps of 10, thumbnail decode target 720 px; carb bounds 0–1000 g; page size 50; error-body log cap 200 chars; onboarding connection-test debounce 1000 ms; watch discovery timeout 15 s, telemetry timeout 10 s, face-push timeout 150 s, result auto-dismiss 5 s, watch update-check cooldown 10 s, watch install timer 15 s; retention slider 1–30 days (default 7); alert thresholds 20–500 mg/dL (defaults 55/70/180/250, staleness 1 h); mmol bounds label 1.1–27.7; MGDL_PER_MMOL 18.0156; debug fast staleness 20 s stale / 45 s too-stale; debug injections 120 and 54 mg/dL, 60 s age, 20 seeded events; BLE debug buffer 100 entries; wear APK download cap 100 MB.

port.subsystem: AI chat, meal logging (Meal Intelligence / Epic 50), onboarding, settings, in-app license viewer, and debug surfaces — iPhone + Apple Watch port of Android `com.glycemicgpt.mobile`

ports_cleanly.capability: AI Chat page state machine and provider probe (Loading → Ready | NoProvider | Offline, no polling, terminal Offline with Retry)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: An observable view model (`@Observable`) with a 4-case Swift enum drives a SwiftUI view. `checkProvider()` runs in `.task {}` on first appearance and on the Retry button. `GET /api/ai/provider` on the 15s URLSession; `HTTPURLResponse.statusCode` 200..<300 → Ready, exactly 404 → NoProvider, any other status or thrown `URLError` → Offline. No auto re-check, no backoff — identical semantics. The whole Chat tab is conditionally excluded from `TabView` when no base URL is configured, and a deep link / restored `NavigationStack` path targeting chat pops to Home. UI test identifiers replace Compose test tags one-for-one (`ai_chat_no_provider`, `ai_chat_offline`).

ports_cleanly.capability: AI Chat message send, in-memory transcript, 2000-char cap, 100-message cap, curated error taxonomy
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `ChatMessage` becomes an `Identifiable` struct with `UUID()`, `Date()`, and an optional non-nil-on-the-wire `disclaimer`. `sendMessage()` guards on trimmed-blank and `isSending`, refuses `> 2000` locally (so exactly 2000 still sends) with no network call, appends and `suffix(100)` on both appends. Transcript stays in memory only — no SwiftData, no persistence — matching Android exactly. Error mapping ports to a `switch` on the thrown error: `URLError.timedOut` → "AI response took too long. Please try again"; other `URLError` (`.notConnectedToInternet`, `.cannotFindHost`, `.networkConnectionLost`, …) → "Check your internet connection and try again"; HTTP 401 → "Session expired. Please sign in again"; HTTP 500...599 → "Server error. Please try again later"; default → "Couldn't get a response. Please try again". Because iOS gives typed status codes rather than a stringified `HTTP 5xx` message, the mapping becomes stricter than Android's regex — same user-visible copy, no raw error ever surfaced. Errors render as an inline dismissible row at the bottom of the list, not an alert.

ports_cleanly.capability: AI Chat screen layout, 4 suggestion chips, markdown rendering with image suppression and link-scheme allowlist, permanent medical footer
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: SwiftUI `ScrollViewReader` + `LazyVStack` with `.scrollTargetLayout()`/`scrollTo(lastID)` reproduces the auto-scroll on `messages.count`/`isSending` change; `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)` + keyboard avoidance replaces `imePadding()`. Chips are a `Flow`-style layout of buttons that only fill the input. Bubbles use `.clipShape(UnevenRoundedRectangle(...))` for the 16/16/16/4 vs 16/16/4/16 asymmetry, `maxWidth: 300`. Markdown: a rendering layer (SwiftUI `AttributedString(markdown:)` covers inline only, so a block-level renderer is needed for headings/lists/tables). The two load-bearing security behaviors port verbatim and must be re-implemented in whichever renderer: strip `![…](…)`, `![…][…]` and `` (case-insensitive) before rendering so AI content can never trigger an outbound image fetch, and open only URLs whose lowercased scheme is `http`/`https` via `openURL`, silently ignoring everything else. Blank markdown renders nothing. The licenses screen's `linkifyMask = 0` equivalent is simply not enabling data detectors there.

ports_cleanly.capability: TTS markdown-stripping pipeline (17 ordered regex passes, table-row flattening, fenced-code-before-inline-code ordering)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A pure Swift function using `NSRegularExpression` (or Swift `Regex` with `.anchorsMatchLineEndings(true)` for the MULTILINE patterns) applied in the exact same order, with the table-row pass using a match-enumerating replacement that splits cells on `|`, trims, and joins with ", ". Order is preserved so a fence's contents are never partially unwrapped. Unit-testable with no platform dependency. The watch keeps its own separate, simpler stripper for on-screen display, as on Android.

ports_cleanly.capability: AI daily brief deliberately NOT an in-app screen — briefs surface only as a distinct notification category
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Preserve the absence: no brief screen, view model, or endpoint. The Android `ai_notifications_v<n>` channel becomes a `UNNotificationCategory` identifier plus a `threadIdentifier` on server-pushed alerts whose type is neither a LOW nor a HIGH type, delivered at `.active` interruption level (never `.critical`/`.timeSensitive`). Onboarding's Features copy and the Settings AI-sound row keep their wording. If a brief surface is ever wanted it is new work, not a port.

ports_cleanly.capability: Meal logging availability gate and page state machine (local cache short-circuit → Disabled with no round trip; server probe as authority)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Same two-layer gate. A locally cached `mealIntelligenceEnabled` flag short-circuits to Disabled with no network call; otherwise `listFoodRecords(limit: 1)` probes, mapping success → Ready, `MealError.featureDisabled` → Disabled, everything else → Offline. Chrome is a `NavigationStack` detail with a large-title-off toolbar and a Back button (the `DetailScaffold` equivalent). All three meal destinations stay registered but redirect to Home when no backend is configured, so a restored navigation path never blanks.

ports_cleanly.capability: Meal photo capture — camera, gallery, permission handling, transient capture files
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Gallery uses SwiftUI `PhotosPicker` (PHPicker-backed), which requires no photo-library permission and, importantly, strips location metadata by default — a privacy improvement over Android. Camera uses `UIImagePickerController(sourceType: .camera)` (or an `AVCaptureSession` sheet) behind `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .video)` with `NSCameraUsageDescription`. Denial is non-fatal and shows the same inline error-colored line, but the retry affordance must deep-link to `UIApplication.openSettingsURLString` because iOS never re-prompts after a denial. The transient capture writes to `NSTemporaryDirectory()/meal_photos/capture_<epochms>.jpg`; single-file delete on cancel/supersession and a full-directory sweep only on `reset()`, exactly as `MealPhotoFiles` does. Button order, copy, and the History / Common foods / Re-log secondary actions are unchanged.

ports_cleanly.capability: Meal photo compression — 1280px longest edge, 5 MiB cap, EXIF orientation applied to pixels, all metadata dropped
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: ImageIO does this more safely than Android: `CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex` with `kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: 1280`, `kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true`, and `kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true` performs the downsample and applies EXIF orientation to pixels in one step without ever decoding the full-resolution bitmap (which also removes Android's power-of-two `inSampleSize` ladder and its OOM exposure). Then the identical JPEG quality ladder: `jpegData(compressionQuality:)` at 0.9 stepping down by 0.1 while over 5 MiB until 0.4, throwing "Image is too large to upload after compression" if still over. Re-encoding drops all EXIF/GPS — the same defense-in-depth privacy guarantee, which must be pinned by a test asserting the uploaded bytes contain no GPS IFD. The 5 MiB client cap must stay ≤ the server's 5 MiB cap.

ports_cleanly.capability: Carb estimate rendering, the non-negotiable verify-before-dosing qualifier, confidence bar, and the merged accessibility phrase
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `VERIFY_BEFORE_DOSING_TEXT` is a single constant reused by all six surfaces (log result pinned above the scroll region, history header, common-foods header, re-log sheet, edit sheet, Home recent-meal card). The soft-amber SafetyPalette becomes an asset-catalog color set with light/dark variants — explicitly not the semantic error/red color. Formatting ports directly: "≈ 40–55 g carbs" collapsing to "≈ 50 g carbs", integer when `truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1) == 0` else one decimal, formatted with `Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")`. The confidence bar is a 120×6 rounded capsule filled 1.0 green / 0.6 amber / 0.3 amber with no bar for UNKNOWN — Medium and Low still distinguished by length, not hue. The accessibility merge is a direct match: `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` with an explicit `.accessibilityLabel` of "Estimated <low> to <high> grams of carbs, <confidence>. <qualifier>.<dispersion note>", so VoiceOver can never read the number without the never-dose qualifier.

ports_cleanly.capability: Multi-sample dispersion (uncertainty) treatment on the create response only
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `MealDispersion` decodes from `estimate_dispersion`, present only on create and absent on history reads. Blank note → nil so nothing renders. `wideSpread || !identityAgreement` renders the visceral caution strip on the SafetyPalette; otherwise a quiet secondary line. Defaults on decode stay `wideSpread = false`, `identityAgreement = true` so a missing field never fabricates a caution. The note appends to the merged accessibility phrase.

ports_cleanly.capability: Food identity confirmation (grounding gate) with the stale-response guard

One normalized candidate value drives both the submission and the enable check. The stale-response guard becomes: capture the record id before `await`, then discard the response if `state.record?.id != requestRecordId` — the same pattern Swift structured concurrency needs anyway. On success, replace the record and null out `audit`/`auditError` because grounding and precedence changed.

ports_cleanly.capability: Carb correction with client-side reject-not-clamp validation shared with common-food edit
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A single `CarbBounds` value type with `min = 0.0`, `max = 1000.0`, and `validate`/`parse` returning the same ordered messages (NaN → negative → >1000 → low>high). `Double(text.trimmed)` replaces `toDoubleOrNull()`; `.keyboardType(.decimalPad)`. ports_cleanly.capability: "How was this estimated" audit / provenance trail (on-demand, invalidated by identity confirmation)

Same record-id pin/discard guard. Loaded on demand only, never eagerly. The model's self-reported confidence stays out of the contract.

ports_cleanly.capability: Glucose-framed nutrition facts (assumed portion, macros with glucose notes, net carbs behind its caveat, section disclaimer)

Macro values render as whole units (`value.rounded()`), net carbs as "≈ 34–49 g" collapsing when the rounded endpoints meet. The section disclaimer renders from the content view, not the card, so a portion-only payload still shows it.

ports_cleanly.capability: Grounding-backed comorbidity nutrition (heart / blood-pressure awareness block)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port including the defensive gating: drop facts with non-finite or negative values; if no fact survives, the entire block maps to nil so an empty card never renders; keep `sugarNote` only when a surviving fact key is `sugars_grams` or `added_sugars_grams`, mirroring the server's `_SUGAR_KEYS`. ports_cleanly.capability: Save as common food (named sheet, server-echoed confirmation, 409 conflict copy)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port. Empty trimmed name → "Give this food a name first." with no API call. `POST /api/food-records/{id}/save-as-common-food`. The confirmation echoes the server-returned name, not the typed one. HTTP 409 → "A common food with that name already exists."

ports_cleanly.capability: Typed meal error taxonomy and full HTTP status → user copy mapping
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A Swift `enum MealError: Error` with the same cases and messages. The response body is `Data`, so Android's single-read constraint disappears. Decode FastAPI's `detail` tolerating both shapes (a `String` or a Pydantic array whose first element's `msg` is used) via a custom `Decodable` union. The full status map ports verbatim (400/404-with-substring-branches/409/413/415/422-with-vision-branch/429/500/502/503/504/default), including the case-insensitive detail substrings "not enabled", "ai provider", "vision" that are pinned by `MealRepositoryTest`. The ≥500 diagnostic log with the 200-char body cap ports to `OSLog` with a privacy-annotated redaction policy equivalent to the release `ReleaseTree` scrubbing; `CancellationError` is always rethrown.

ports_cleanly.capability: Meal history screen (fixed page size 50, no pagination, no local cache, terminal offline state, optimistic delete)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port including the render priority (disabled → loading → terminal error when the list is empty → qualifier + list) and the deliberate refusal to show "No meals logged yet." while the backend is unreachable. Job supersession uses a stored `Task` cancelled on reload, and the post-`await` `isActive` check becomes an explicit `try Task.checkCancellation()` / `guard !Task.isCancelled` after the call — the same hazard exists in Swift when a repository maps errors into a `Result`. Delete has no confirmation, optimistic row removal, failure surfaced as a transient bottom banner (the Snackbar equivalent).

ports_cleanly.capability: Common Foods screen (list, read-only re-log sheet, edit with embedded qualifier, delete)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port, including the documented v1 limitation that Re-log is read-only because the API has no create-record-from-common-food path. The re-log sheet renders the qualifier, `CarbEstimateContent` with UNKNOWN confidence (so no confidence bar), the "verify before dosing — no new photo needed" copy, and a single Close. The edit sheet embeds the qualifier (on iOS a sheet dims the presenting view the same way an AlertDialog scrim does) and its body scrolls so Dynamic Type at accessibility sizes cannot clip the buttons — which is a stronger requirement on iOS than on Android.

ports_cleanly.capability: Onboarding 5-page pager with the un-swipeable safety-acknowledgement gate
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A paged container (page-style `TabView` with scrolling disabled from the disclaimer page onward, or a manual offset pager) preserving the exact gate: pages 0–1 swipe freely, and from the disclaimer page only the explicit "I Understand" button advances. Start page selection stays SERVER only when a saved base URL exists AND onboarding was previously completed, else WELCOME. Page indicators, Skip/Back/Next slot logic, and all five disclaimer cards port verbatim — including the Story 50.S photo-carb card that names the prohibited action, which is required consent coverage for the AI-vision feature.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings screen composition, section order, and reload-on-resume lifecycle
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A single `Form`/`ScrollView` with the same section order and the same header treatment. `LifecycleEventEffect(ON_RESUME)` becomes `.onChange(of: scenePhase)` reacting to `.active` plus an initial `.task`. The auth-state collector becomes an async sequence over the auth store that drops the first value and de-duplicates. Sheets/alerts for Sign Out, Unpair, Deactivate Plugin, Remove Plugin, and Insecure HTTP live at the bottom. The plugin-boundary `catch (Throwable)` discipline is unnecessary on iOS because drivers are compile-time-linked, but each driver metadata/descriptor read should still be independently failure-isolated so a descriptor failure drops only the notes.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings Account section (server URL, connection test, sign in/out, logout ordering)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port of both the logged-in and logged-out layouts and all copy. `saveBaseUrl` keeps the same three branches (blank → clear without persisting; invalid → set the message without persisting; valid → persist and recompute `backendConfigured` in the same state update so the alert-threshold editor flips read-only in the same frame). The load-bearing logout ordering ports exactly: stop the alert stream → bump the session generation → clear the token → clear safety limits, BACKEND thresholds only, analytics, pump profile → reset per-account preferences → best-effort device unregistration. Credentials and the refresh token move to Keychain (see the notification/Keychain requirement about accessibility class). The brittle `contains("successfully")` coloring should be replaced with an explicit success flag on the result — a behavior-preserving fix, not a redesign.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings Sync section (backend sync toggle hidden in BLE-only mode, data retention slider 1–30 days)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port. The Backend Sync card is hidden whenever no backend is configured; the Data Retention card always renders. The slider is `1...30` with `step: 1`, committing on editing-ended, coerced into 1...30 both in the setter and again in the store. Default stays 7 days, and the value continues to bound the selectable analysis windows on Home.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings Meal Intelligence section (per-account toggle, request-version stale guard, honest sync-failure copy, fail-closed on 401/403)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Direct port. The whole section (header, card, trailing spacer) is omitted when no backend is configured. The local cache is written first so the Home entry point hides/shows instantly through an observable stream. The monotonically increasing request version plus `Task` cancellation ports directly to Swift concurrency, including the rule that the version is bumped and the in-flight task cancelled even when no new request is launched. Failure keeps the optimistic value and shows "Saved on this device. Couldn't sync to your account." Both the PATCH and the GET fail closed on 401/403 by writing the local cache to false; transient/network failures keep the cached value. Store default stays ON.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings alert thresholds editor (SAFETY-CRITICAL): read-only under a backend, editable in BLE-only mode, full validation and unit handling
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Pure logic — ports exactly. Read-only rendering, the "Waiting for the first sync from your server." state, and the error-colored "On-device alarms are OFF until you set all four thresholds." all port. Parsing: trim, replace "," with ".", `Double(_:)`, reject non-finite; mg/dL rounds to Int, mmol/L multiplies by 18.0156 then rounds; canonical storage is always mg/dL. Validation order and copy are unchanged, including the computed mmol bounds label 1.1–27.7 derived so the quoted values themselves round back into 20...500. `saveLocalAlertThresholds` re-checks backend-configured state live, not the cached UI flag. Two iOS-specific storage requirements: the threshold store must be readable by the alert engine while the device is locked, so it must be a file written atomically with `.completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication` data protection (not `.complete`) — `UserDefaults` in an App Group is acceptable but the protection class must be verified; and the synchronous `commit()` durability property becomes an atomic file write completed before the save returns.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings Appearance — theme mode and glucose units (including the one-time seed notice and the canonical 18.0156 constant)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `ThemeMode` (System/Dark/Light) is per-device, persisted by name, corrupt values falling back to System, applied via `.preferredColorScheme`. The fixed non-Material-You palettes become asset-catalog color sets with light/dark variants. `safetyPalette()`'s luminance check becomes a read of the environment `colorScheme`, which correctly tracks a forced theme because `.preferredColorScheme` sets that environment value. Glucose unit selection, the optimistic local write, the backend PATCH with server-resolved fold-back, the honest sync-failure copy, the BLE-only no-PATCH path, and the dismissible seed notice with its best-effort acknowledge POST all port directly. `MGDL_PER_MMOL = 18.0156` stays the single constant; mg/dL renders as an integer, mmol/L as one decimal with `en_US_POSIX`; conversion happens once from the most precise mg/dL source and rounds last (70→3.9, 180→10.0, 120→6.7, 100→5.6). A spread must use the offset-free `convertSpread`.

ports_cleanly.capability: Settings Developer section (debug-only fault injection toggles, hard-gated in release)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: The whole section is wrapped in `#if DEBUG` so it is compiled out of release entirely — a stronger guarantee than Android's R8 elimination. The `simulateBackendUnreachable` and `debugFastStaleness` getters/setters keep their belt-and-braces `#if DEBUG` gating at the store level too. The reactive stream that lets the alert stream force-drop its connection the instant the fault flips ports as an `AsyncStream`; the same rationale holds on iOS (an injected transport fault only affects new requests, so a healthy long-lived stream would otherwise stay connected). The fast-staleness policy swap (20s stale / 45s too-stale) ports unchanged.

ports_cleanly.capability: BLE Debug Console screen (debug builds only, CGM injection, sync-queue seeding, TX/RX log)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Compiled under `#if DEBUG` and reachable only from the debug Settings section. The injection constants port verbatim (120 mg/dL, 54 mg/dL, 60s age, 20 seeded events, 100-entry circular buffer). `injectCgm` keeps its independent `#if DEBUG` guard because it writes to the same local store that drives the real glucose hero and can fire a real local notification, and it must drive the same production seam the real poll path uses so the watch relay and alert floor see it identically. This screen becomes disproportionately more valuable on iOS: Core Bluetooth does not exist in the Simulator, so injection is the only way to exercise the alert floor, the watch relay, and the honest-degradation surfaces in the developer's Simulator loop. Recommend extending the same philosophy with a debug "use a bundled sample meal photo" injector, since the Simulator has no camera.

ports_cleanly.capability: In-app Open Source Licenses viewer (bundled assets, offline, plain-text license bodies, selection across paragraphs, restored scroll position)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Assets ship as bundle resources read off the main actor; a read failure yields the Unavailable state with "License text could not be read from this build." in error color (a packaging failure, not a user state). The scroll position is hoisted above the loading branch so a rotation or size-class change returns the reader to their place. One `.textSelection(.enabled)` applied to the whole `LazyVStack` so selection crosses paragraph boundaries. Same item order and same rule that license texts render as plain text, never markdown, because numbered clauses parse as list markers. `stripUnresolvableLinks` ports (repo-relative markdown links reduce to their label; scheme-carrying targets such as `mailto:` are left alone). The Gradle `generateLicenseAssets`/`generateDependencyAttribution` pair becomes an Xcode build phase or SwiftPM build-tool plugin that regenerates the five documents on every build from README's `## License` section (a missing heading must fail the build), LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md, and the resolved release dependency set (`Package.resolved` plus any vendored/XCFramework licenses) — preserving the invariant that a dependency cannot enter the build without entering the attribution. An empty source document must fail the build rather than ship a blank section. The screen still states nothing of its own and works with no connectivity.

ports_cleanly.capability: Navigation, backend-mode gating, session banner, and shared spoke chrome
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `TabView` with [Home, (Chat only when a backend is configured), Alerts, Settings]; spoke destinations (`meal_log`, `meal_history`, `common_foods`, `licenses`, `ble_debug`, `pairing`, detail screens) live in a `NavigationStack` with the shared toolbar + Back chrome and hide the tab bar. The backend-gated routes stay registered so a restored `NavigationPath` or deep link does not blank, and render a guard that pops to the Home root — the guard must read the mode from live observable state, not a captured value, exactly as Android's `State<Boolean>` fix does. The session banner renders for Expired unconditionally and for Unauthenticated only when a backend is configured (a BLE-only user is permanently unauthenticated by design), and tapping it navigates to Settings. Start destination is keyed on onboarding completion alone. Logout navigates to Onboarding clearing the entire stack.

needs_redesign.capability: AI Chat text-to-speech output and voice picker
needs_redesign.why: `AVSpeechSynthesizer` provides speech, but the voice metadata model is different enough that the Android voice-picker logic cannot be transliterated. iOS voice identifiers look like `com.apple.voice.compact.en-US.Samantha`, so the Android display-name derivation (text after `x-`, then after the last `-`, then last 3 chars) produces garbage. There is no `isNetworkConnectionRequired` flag, so the "Online" suffix has no source; quality is an enum (`.default`/`.enhanced`/`.premium`) not an Int, so the `quality >= 400` → "HD" rule needs remapping. Siri voices are not exposed to third-party apps, and Personal Voice requires a separate `AVSpeechSynthesizer.requestPersonalVoiceAuthorization` consent. Additionally, iOS requires explicit `AVAudioSession` configuration (category, and a ducking/mixing policy) that Android's TTS engine does not, and the persisted `ai_tts_voice` values from Android will never resolve on iOS.
options: Enumerate `AVSpeechSynthesisVoice.speechVoices()` filtered to the device language, sort by (quality descending, locale, name), and derive the display name from `voice.name` + `Locale.current.localizedString(forRegionCode:)` — e.g. "United States - Samantha (HD)" where HD means `.enhanced` or `.premium`. Drop the Online suffix as unrepresentable.
Offer only the system default voice and drop the picker entirely, keeping just the on/off toggle.
Add Personal Voice as an opt-in extra entry behind its own authorization prompt.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Take the first option. Keep the exact toggle interaction (tap while off enables immediately; tap while on opens a menu whose first item is "Disable TTS", then a divider, then voices with a checkmark on the selected one), keep the persisted keys `ai_tts_enabled` (default false) / `ai_tts_voice` (default empty = system), keep the fallback to the system voice when a persisted identifier is absent, and keep the inseparable safety behavior: the spoken string is always `response + ". This is not medical advice."` run through the markdown stripper, skipped when blank, spoken with the queue flushed. Configure `AVAudioSession` with `.playback`, `.duckOthers`, and `.spokenAudio` mode, and deactivate with `.notifyOthersOnDeactivation` when speech ends. Do not add Personal Voice for v1. Voice/TTS settings remain a single shared pair that the phone pushes to the watch, as on Android.

needs_redesign.capability: AI chat network transport — the 90s long-inference request surviving app suspension
needs_redesign.why: The two-client timeout split itself is trivial on iOS (two `URLSessionConfiguration`s: 15s `timeoutIntervalForRequest`/`timeoutIntervalForResource` vs 90s, with `httpMaximumConnectionsPerHost = 2` mirroring `ConnectionPool(2, 90s)`, and the chat session excluded from the reachability/network-health monitor for the same documented reason). The genuine problem is lifecycle: on Android the ViewModel and process typically survive a backgrounded 90-second LLM call. On iOS the app is suspended within seconds of backgrounding, and in-flight tasks on a default `URLSession` fail. `beginBackgroundTask` buys roughly 30 seconds, not 90. So the Android behavior — send a question, switch apps, come back to the answer — does not survive a straight port.
options: Accept the narrower contract: an in-flight chat request is cancelled when the app leaves the foreground, and the UI says so honestly on return ("Your question was interrupted. Send it again."). Simplest, and matches the fact that the transcript is in-memory only anyway.

Use a background `URLSessionConfiguration` for the chat request so the response is delivered via `handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession` even after suspension — but this requires persisting at least the pending request so the delivered response has somewhere to land, which breaks the in-memory-only transcript invariant.
Keep the default session but wrap the send in `beginBackgroundTask` to extend the window to ~30s, which helps short answers and not long ones.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Ship option 1 for the phone chat screen: preserve the in-memory-only transcript exactly as Android has it, cancel on background, and add explicit honest copy on return. It is the only option that does not introduce chat persistence, and the chat screen is a foreground, attended experience. Use a background `URLSession` only for the watch-relay path (see the watch relay entry), where the user is not looking at the phone by definition. Keep the 15s/90s split and keep the debug simulate-unreachable fault applied to the chat session so the fault toggle still exercises chat.

needs_redesign.capability: Watch AI chat relay (phone side) — replacing WearChatRelayService
needs_redesign.why: Every mechanism this service depends on is Android-only. There are no foreground services on iOS, so there is no way to hold the process up for a 90-second call on demand and no ongoing "Processing watch request" notification. `WCSession.sendMessage` from the watch will wake a suspended iOS counterpart app in the background, but the woken app gets a short, unguaranteed execution window — nowhere near 90 seconds — and `replyHandler` has its own timeout. Blocking a thread deliberately (Android's `runBlocking` on the binder thread) has no safe analogue. Separately, the relay exists on Android partly because Wear OS network access is unreliable; on watchOS the app is independent since watchOS 6 and its `URLSession` works over LTE, Wi-Fi, or transparently through the paired iPhone, so most of the relay's reason for existing disappears.
options: Make the watch app call `/api/ai/chat` directly with its own `URLSession`, storing the access/refresh token in the watch's own Keychain, provisioned from the phone via `WCSession.updateApplicationContext`/`transferUserInfo` (Keychain access groups do not span devices, so the token must be transferred, not shared).

Keep a phone relay, but implement it as a background `URLSession` upload task started from `session(_:didReceiveMessage:)` and deliver the answer back with `transferUserInfo` (queued and guaranteed) rather than a reply handler.
Shorten the server-side chat timeout for watch-originated requests so the whole round trip fits inside a reply-handler window.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Do option 1 as the primary path and option 2 as the fallback when the watch reports no independent connectivity. Preserve every piece of the relay's behavior contract regardless of transport: reject empty input; reject >500 characters with "Message too long (max 500 chars)"; and when no server is configured return the terminal copy "AI chat needs a GlycemicGPT server — none is set up on your phone." verbatim, checked before any work begins and deliberately never saying "try again". Port `sanitizeErrorMessage` unchanged (timeout / no internet / session expired / server error / generic). Drop the foreground-service notification and the reference counting — they have no iOS meaning. Fix the existing 30s-watch-vs-90s-phone mismatch while you are here by aligning the watch's watchdog with the actual request timeout. The alert-dismiss path ports as a `WCSession` message that acknowledges locally first (so a cleared alert on the watch is truthful when the backend is unreachable) and carries the alert id, closing the documented Android bug where an empty payload can acknowledge the wrong alert.

needs_redesign.capability: Watch AI chat UI and the watch-face chat launcher
needs_redesign.why: The screen's logic ports, but two mechanisms do not. Voice input: watchOS has no `RecognizerIntent`; text entry is the system input controller (dictation, Scribble, and the keyboard on Series 7+), presented via SwiftUI `TextFieldLink` or `presentTextInputController`, which runs out of process — so there is no "recognizer missing" case and no microphone/speech usage description needed from the app. Launcher: watchOS has no third-party watch faces, so the Android `ChatComplicationDataSource` becomes a WidgetKit accessory widget (`accessoryCircular`/`accessoryCorner`) that the user places on an Apple face, plus a Smart Stack widget, both deep-linking into the chat view via `widgetURL`.
options: SwiftUI `TextFieldLink` presenting the system input controller (dictation + Scribble + keyboard), with the same 500-character truncation and the same blank-input copy.

Add an in-app `SFSpeechRecognizer` flow for a custom voice UI — requires `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` and `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`, adds two permission prompts, and is strictly worse than the system control.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Use the system input controller. Keep the whole `Idle | Loading | Success | Error` machine, the optional prefill from the widget deep link truncated to 500 characters, the three quick-query buttons ("How am I doing?", "Breakfast advice", "Why is my BG high?"), the blue accent on the ask button, the loading watchdog, the one-question-one-answer no-transcript model, the simpler on-watch markdown stripper, the disclaimer in small caption text defaulting to "Not medical advice. Consult your doctor." when blank, and the TTS speaking `response + ". This is not medical advice."` guarded against re-speaking the same response. Clearing chat state on leaving while loading ports directly to `.onDisappear`.

needs_redesign.capability: Meal photo upload lifecycle — supersession, error recovery, and the uncatchable out-of-memory path
needs_redesign.why: Job supersession, the previous-capture sweep, the retained current photo for the thumbnail, and the typed failure routing all port cleanly to structured concurrency. One behavior does not: Android catches `OutOfMemoryError` and shows "That photo is too large to process. Try a smaller one." On iOS there is no catchable out-of-memory condition — the system jetsams the process. The stated safety property ("the Estimating carbs… spinner can never get permanently stuck") therefore has to be achieved by prevention plus crash-recovery rather than by a catch block.
options: Prevent the condition: use ImageIO thumbnail downsampling so the full-resolution bitmap is never decoded at all, which removes the realistic OOM path for phone-camera and library images.
Add a defensive pre-check on source pixel dimensions (from `CGImageSourceCopyPropertiesAtIndex`, which reads headers only) and refuse absurd images up front with the Android copy.

Persist a small 'upload in progress' marker so that if the app is jetsammed mid-compression, the next launch clears it and shows an honest 'That photo couldn't be processed' state instead of resuming into a spinner.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Do all three: ImageIO downsampling as the primary prevention, a header-only dimension pre-check reusing the exact Android copy so the message still exists as a user-facing state, and the launch-time marker so a jetsam cannot leave a stuck medical spinner behind. Everything else ports verbatim — cancel the in-flight task before starting a new one so a previous capture's file is never deleted out from under an active read; delete the previous capture off the main actor; three-way failure routing (`CancellationError` rethrown / prevented-OOM copy / "Couldn't read that photo. Try another one."); multipart part name `file`, filename `meal.jpg`, `image/jpeg`, posted on the 90s session; and VISION / NO_PROVIDER as dead-end states with a Back button that calls `reset()` rather than retryable errors.

needs_redesign.capability: Home meal glance — the draggable, position-persisting meal FAB
needs_redesign.why: The Recent Meal card ports unchanged. The draggable extended FAB does not belong on iOS: there is no FAB idiom, a free-floating draggable control conflicts with the tab bar, the Home indicator safe area, and Dynamic Type layout, and its per-device saved position plus the VoiceOver "Reset position to default" custom action exist purely to compensate for Android's drag being pointer-only. Keeping it would be porting an Android accommodation rather than the capability.
options: A fixed floating action button pinned bottom-trailing above the tab bar safe area, no drag, with the same label and camera icon.
A toolbar/nav-bar item plus a prominent 'Log a meal' row at the top of the Home list.
A persistent bottom accessory attached to the tab bar (current iOS supports a bottom accessory slot on TabView).
Faithfully reimplement drag with `DragGesture`, touch-slop-based tap disambiguation, live-container-size clamping, and per-device persistence.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Ship option 1 with option 2's list row as a redundant entry point, and drop drag entirely. This preserves what the drag existed to protect (the button never obscuring content, and reachability) using layout instead of user labor: the button sits above the tab bar and the Home content keeps its bottom inset so the last card is never covered. Keep every gate: the button is absent when no backend is configured and absent when meal intelligence is locally off; a transient/offline probe failure keeps it visible (only `featureDisabled` hides it) so the meal screen can show its own degraded state; and the setting is re-checked on both the success and failure paths so a toggle flipped mid-flight cannot re-expose it. Keep the Recent Meal card exactly as-is, including the neutral placeholder thumbnail (the backend returns no image) and the embedded verify-before-dosing qualifier.

needs_redesign.capability: Onboarding server setup, connection test, and the inline insecure-LAN-HTTP opt-in
needs_redesign.why: The form, debounce, and test flow port, but the cleartext story does not. iOS App Transport Security blocks `http://` at the URLSession layer before the app's own policy runs, and ATS cannot be scoped to private IP ranges (see the impossible entry). Separately, iOS 14+ Local Network Privacy means any connection to an RFC1918 address, a `.local` name, or the link-local range triggers a one-time system permission prompt; the app must declare `NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription`, and if the user denies it, connections to a LAN server fail with an opaque error and cannot be re-prompted in-app. That is a second, independent failure mode the Android flow has no equivalent for, and it is the single most likely reason a self-hoster's first connection test fails on iOS.
options: Set `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads = YES` (with no `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` key, which would override it) and keep `UrlSecurityPolicy` as the sole in-app guard, exactly as Android already does.
Ship https-only on iOS and remove the insecure-LAN-HTTP opt-in, directing self-hosters to a reverse proxy, a self-signed certificate the user trusts, or a mesh VPN.
Ship `NSAllowsLocalNetworking = YES` only, which covers `.local` names and link-local addresses but not 10.x / 172.16.x / 192.168.x — i.e. it covers mDNS but not the common case.
needs_redesign.recommendation: See the PM question — the ATS posture is a genuine product/review-risk call. Whichever posture is chosen, the flow itself must gain a Local Network permission step: request it before or during the first connection test, and when it is denied say so specifically ("iOS is blocking access to devices on your local network. Turn on Local Network for GlycemicGPT in Settings.") with a Settings deep link, never a generic "Connection failed". Everything else ports verbatim: the 1000ms debounce after validation, the shared `INVALID_URL_MESSAGE`, persisting the typed URL before the test so the request layer routes to it and restoring the previous known-good URL on failure, the acknowledgement dialog carrying `INSECURE_HTTP_RISK_TEXT` word-for-word, confirming re-running the test with the debounce forced so the flow proceeds without a second tap, and editing the URL clearing both the result and the opt-in affordance. The inline opt-in must stay inline because a fresh install still cannot reach Settings before signing in.

needs_redesign.capability: Onboarding login, BLE-only entry, notification permission, and completion
needs_redesign.why: The form, validation, error copy, password wiping, and the load-bearing cancel-then-clear ordering in `continueWithoutServer()` all port. Two things change materially. First, iOS presents the notification authorization prompt exactly once per install; a denial is permanent until the user visits Settings, and any options you want (`.criticalAlert`, `.timeSensitive`-capable delivery, `.provisional`) must be requested in that single call — you cannot come back later and ask for critical alerts. That makes the request's composition a one-shot, safety-critical decision rather than the routine runtime permission it is on Android. Second, credential storage moves to Keychain, and the accessibility class is a correctness decision, not a detail: `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked` would make the token unreadable while the phone is locked, silently breaking overnight token refresh and any background work the alert path depends on.
options: Request `[.alert, .sound, .badge, .criticalAlert]` in one call at the end of both completion paths, exactly where Android requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS.
Split the requests — ask for standard notifications at onboarding and critical alerts later at first low-alert configuration. iOS permits only one prompt, so the second request would silently no-op.
Use `.provisional` authorization to avoid the prompt entirely — but provisional notifications are delivered quietly to Notification Center, which is disqualifying for a life-safety alarm.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 1. Request the full option set including `.criticalAlert` at the end of both completion paths (after login and after "Use without a server (BLE-only)"), because the Android comment applies with more force on iOS: the on-device alert floor is silently suppressed without notification permission, so a user could believe they are monitored when they are not. If the critical-alerts entitlement is not yet granted, requesting `.criticalAlert` is harmless. Keep the ordering property — resolve the permission before flipping the navigate flag, so the prompt does not race the navigation transition. Store the access token, refresh token, and expiry in Keychain with `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock`, in a shared access group with the widget/notification-service extensions. Keep the start-destination policy keyed on onboarding completion alone, deliberately independent of session validity, so an expired refresh token cannot lock locally-cached pump data behind an impossible login. Keep clearing the password from state on both success and failure.

needs_redesign.capability: Settings Network section, the URL security policy, and the app-wide insecure-transport banner
needs_redesign.why: `UrlSecurityPolicy` is pure logic and ports line-for-line to Swift — the strict canonical IPv4 parser (rejecting octal, hex, bare-decimal, leading zeros, >255 octets), the IPv6 parser including IPv4-mapped classification, the `.local` exception requiring a label, and the deliberate refusal to ever perform DNS. What changes is that on iOS this policy is no longer the sole guard: ATS sits underneath it and will reject cleartext before the policy is consulted unless ATS is configured to allow it, and Local Network Privacy sits alongside it and can block the connection entirely regardless of scheme. So the app now has three independent gates where Android had one, and the user-facing state must distinguish them or every LAN failure will look the same.
options: Port the policy verbatim and add two new user-visible conditions to the Network card: ATS posture (build-level, informational) and Local Network permission state (actionable, with a Settings deep link).
Use `NWPathMonitor`/`NWConnection` to pre-flight local reachability and surface a specific error before issuing the HTTP request.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Do both. Port `UrlSecurityPolicy` unchanged including `isAllowed`, `isBlockedPendingLanOptIn`, and `isActiveInsecureHttp` — note the Android method is `isBlockedPendingLanOptIn`, not `isBlockedPendingLanHttpOptIn` as the map states. Keep the toggle semantics exactly: enabling routes through the acknowledgement dialog and only confirmation persists it; disabling is immediate; the setting is per-device and survives logout because the LAN box is the same across sign-ins. Keep the app-wide banner driven reactively by the cross-product of the opt-in flag and the base URL through `isActiveInsecureHttp`, so it lights only when cleartext would actually be sent and never for a public `http://` URL the request layer rejects — and keep it rendering above every screen including onboarding. Add a second, distinct banner or card state for "Local Network access denied", because that condition is invisible in the Simulator and will otherwise be misdiagnosed as a server problem.

needs_redesign.capability: Settings Plugins section — pump card and driver activation
needs_redesign.why: The pump card, its generic (no hardcoded vendor id) driver lookup, the paired/not-paired state, the informational notes reduced from the driver's settings descriptor, the re-pair/unpair/pair buttons, and the unpair confirmation all port. The plugin model underneath does not: iOS forbids dynamic code loading, so drivers are compile-time-linked Swift modules. "Available plugins" becomes a static registry of built-in drivers that can be enabled/disabled, and "activate" means selecting a driver, not loading one. The runtime/custom plugin card is impossible and is listed separately.
options: A compile-time driver registry with per-driver enable/disable, keeping the deactivate confirmation dialog and the derived visibility rules.

Drop activation entirely and auto-select a driver by discovered device — loses the user's ability to deactivate a driver, which the Android confirmation copy treats as safety-relevant ('may stop glucose monitoring').
needs_redesign.recommendation: Option 1. Preserve the safety behaviors: deactivation always routes through the confirmation dialog with the same copy, and the derived-visibility rule ports (a source plugin that only makes sense with a backend is hidden in BLE-only mode unless it is already active, so Deactivate stays reachable). Keep the visibility as a derived/computed property rather than filtering at mutation sites so it cannot go stale against the driver list, active set, and backend mode. Keep the per-driver failure isolation so a descriptor read failure drops only the notes while the card survives. Version strings come from the driver module's own metadata.

needs_redesign.why: On Android there is effectively one axis: POST_NOTIFICATIONS granted or not. On iOS `UNUserNotificationCenter.getNotificationSettings()` reports many independent axes that can each silently suppress an alarm — `authorizationStatus`, `alertSetting`, `soundSetting`, `criticalAlertSetting`, `lockScreenSetting`, `notificationCenterSetting`, `timeSensitiveSetting`, and `scheduledDeliverySetting` (the Notification Summary, which can delay a non-time-sensitive notification by hours). A straight port of "Enabled / Disabled" would report Enabled while the alarm is muted, summarized, or Focus-suppressed — which directly violates the subsystem's honest-degradation contract.
options: Expand the card to report each suppressing condition separately, each with its own Settings deep link.
Report a single derived 'alerts will/will not reach you' verdict computed from all axes, with a disclosure for the detail.
Port the binary card as-is and accept silent suppression.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Options 1 and 2 combined: a single prominent verdict line in error color when anything would suppress a low alarm — keeping the Android voice, e.g. "Disabled — alerts will not appear on your phone" for the denied case — plus an itemized list of the specific conditions (sound off, critical alerts not allowed, Scheduled Summary on, Time Sensitive not allowed). Re-check on every foreground transition so returning from Settings updates it. The Enable button opens `UIApplication.openNotificationSettingsURLString` on iOS 16+, falling back to `openSettingsURLString`, with the same toast-equivalent fallback copy if the URL cannot be opened. Option 3 is not acceptable for this app.

needs_redesign.capability: Settings alert sounds and the low-alert volume boost
needs_redesign.why: iOS has no ringtone picker API, no per-channel sound model, and no way to raise system volume — those specific mechanisms are listed as impossible. But the user-facing capability (choose how each alert category sounds; make low alarms loud and unmissable) is achievable in a different shape. Sounds must be files bundled in the app (or in the app container's Library/Sounds), in Linear PCM / MA4 / µLaw / aLaw packaged as .aiff/.wav/.caf, and ≤30 seconds, referenced per notification request via `UNNotificationSound`. Bypassing Focus and the silent switch requires `.critical` interruption level, the `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.critical-alerts` entitlement (granted only by Apple on request), and the user having granted the `.criticalAlert` authorization option. The freely-available `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive` entitlement with `.timeSensitive` interruption level breaks through Focus if the user permits, but not through the silent switch or a low volume.
options: Ship a curated set of bundled alert sounds per category (a genuinely aggressive alarm set for lows, a notification set for highs and AI) plus an explicit Silent option for AI, with in-app preview playback.

Apply for the critical-alerts entitlement and, when granted, deliver low and high alerts at `.critical` interruption level with `UNNotificationSound.criticalSoundNamed(_:withAudioVolume:)`, where the volume-boost toggle maps to audio volume 1.0 versus a lower value.
If the entitlement is refused, fall back to `.timeSensitive` and change the copy to say plainly that the phone's silent switch and volume can silence the alarm.

Keep an audio session alive in the background to play alarm audio directly (the approach some open-source CGM apps use) — this needs the `audio` background mode, is fragile, and draws App Review scrutiny for a non-audio app.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Options 1 + 2, with 3 as the documented fallback. Reject option 4. Preserve the section's structure: three category rows (Low Glucose Alert / High Glucose Alert / AI Notification) with the same labels and descriptions, the AI row showing a Silent option and hidden entirely in BLE-only mode because AI notifications are backend-generated. Replace the ringtone picker with a bundled-sound list plus preview. Replace "Boost Volume for Lows" with a control whose copy is honest about what iOS actually guarantees; keep the invariant that low and high alerts always attempt Focus bypass independent of the volume control, and keep low alerts re-alerting on each update while highs and AI alert once (on iOS, distinct request identifiers per low update rather than `setOnlyAlertOnce(false)`). The entire versioned-channel-recreation machinery, its lock, and the non-atomic increment hazard simply disappear, because iOS sound is a per-request property — a real simplification.
